Honestly, I wasnt expecting much coming back to this game for achievement hunt(after abandoning the game as soon as I got the tf2 hat), but I was plesantly surprised by it. 

Its a surprisingly well made top down shooter, that does some cool things, some alright things, but has one(and a half) major flaw about it.

Starting with the positives, the gameplay is surprisingly complex, and different from other "top down shooters where you fight aliens" (aka alien breed trilogy and shadowgrounds duology). 

First, you have 8 characters to chose from, 2 per role, and while their star differences are small, I think its actually for the better, because it means you cant accidentally mess up by picking "wrong" one. 

Second positive is weapon variety, while not all are viable, and some have very similar roles to each other(like a railgun and sniper rifle), most do serve different purpose and niche, Like tesla gun, which sucks to farm for its achievement, because its a utility gun, that makes any swarm stop in their track(making it fantastic vs shield bugs) or grenade launcher that is last wep you unlock, that servers both as crowd control and dps gun, but is dangerous to use up close, where you take tons of self dmg, or turrets which serve as tech guy/area defense. Best example of wep variety has to be two healing tools, one is a heal beacon, another is medi gun, and while medi gun is better, heal beacon has its use in uncoordinated teams that looses its hp fast or with med bots, who are better used with heal beacons. This also applies to not just regular weapons, but for offhanded tools as well, where you have weld gun that helps seal doors to prevent swarm from chasing you, or ice grenade for fast crowd control/shield bug weakening, or medkit to get extra heals. 

Enemy variety is also decent, but probably weakest part of the gameplay. Lastly, there's no proper story to speak of. Technically its there, with a few monologues from some guy, and some "lore" books on ground, but its nothing of substance, plus its gameplay first kinda game so I didnt include story in the negatives section.

The one BIG flaw of the game, that could've put this game into "not recommended" category if it was sold for cash is, lack of content. This game has a SINGLE campaign, 7 missions and its done. For a tech demo its fine, but damn, the graphics, the gameplay balancing all suggests finished product... with less than 2 hours of content(way less if you find good team to do final missions, most missions take maybe 9-20 min give or take). Despite how short it is, it will probably take you more hours to finish whole campaign, because even on normal difficulty, it can be challenging when you first start it. Depending on your luck though, you may find one or two pros to carry you.

Earlier I mentioned that the game has one(and a half) flaw, the second and a half flaw being is that its technically co op game, so its way less fun to play solo or with bots. You can use bots, but they arent a bright bunch, you have to almost wrangle them with spamming (GO) button, constantly baby sit em, because if they get surrounded by swarm, they're likely dead meat. They arent enabled by default btw, you have to use console commands to summon them, which is weird because bots have dedicated button(like pressing 2,3,4 to activate their 2nd tools like ammo satchel or heal beam or turret, or if you dont give them those tools, they'll use their offhand tool on press of those buttons) to use their abilities? 

Last thing to note is the achievement hunt, incase you want to do completionist clean up on steam like I did. Is it worth it? Well, kinda? Its not difficult one, the only two semi problems are a few hard achievements that I doubt are doable solo(speedrun achievements n brutal difficulty) and grind achievement. Hard ones are smaller issue because, despite its lack of popularity, this game still has some players play it? Mostly new players who only play it cus its free game or for tf2 hat. But I did find a few veterans sometimes play it, so maybe some will help you out like they did for me. The actualy bad achievement is the grind one, where you have to kill 100,000 swarm, to explain why its so tedious... By the time you finish completing 99% of other achievements, you'll just barely finish grinding the 2nd grindiest achievement, you wont even be 30% done with grindiest achievement, when you do literally everything else, I even got almost all but one prestige medals(medals where, upon reaching max level you can reset level to one, this relocks all your unlocks, but you get shiny medal for it).

My final thoughts on this game: This game had a huge potential that wasnt realised. Fans eventually made their own, sort of remaster, sort of continuation called alien swarm reactive drop, which you can check out on steam(its a free game) if you liked this one, and while its likely the direction this game would've went if Valve kept updating it, I think there was an even cooler, more ambitious idea unrealised. The fact that devs programmed bots to utilise their tools in 2nd hand(like heal beacons) or offhand tools(like hornet rockets) makes me wish they went deeper into mechanics of controlling bots. This could've been a sort of "xcom but in real time, where you have to constantly control your character, and wrangle commands for the other 3 bot teammates". One button could be to split a team of 6 into groups of 2(in the game you only have 4 people limit, but lets say it was 6 like in xcom), you send in your heavy hitter heavy weapons with techie, while the other 4 go clear main entrance, then shield bug(or something worse) shows up, then you command the group of two to stand behind shield bug, while you aggro him, and medbot heals you. But alas we just got, alright or even good top down shooter that, just doesnt have enough content to be replayable for most.

Meh!

reviews.review:
I only started playing this game to get a hat for TF2, but in that time I discovered that this seemingly empty game still had some life left in it. People eventually joined, some left and in the end I made a new friend, as we both worked together as a duo to get through the campaigns missions. Controller support took a tad bit of getting used to, and it didnt properly show what buttons to press so I often resorted to using both my controller and my keyboard in unison, but it didnt subtract from the overall experience...And let me say, what an inspired experience this game is, its pretty refreshing and unique for being a game almost as old as myself, and I will be returning to this game to find more of the worldbuilding...I wonder why this game, especially with what players would have come from TF2, doesnt get far more love and have a bigger playerbase. 

All in all, 9/10 and the melee system felt fantastic
